judged_text: In updateEvent, when externalCalendarId is falsy the selectedCalendar is computed as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which searches for an externalId equal to a falsy value and can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the update is sent with calendarId undefined. For bookings whose stored reference has no externalCalendarId (all pre-refactor bookings, and the fallback path where CalendarManager returns externalId undefined), calendar.events.update receives no calendarId, Google rejects the call, and rescheduling/edits of existing bookings fail with a Google API error where the old code resolved the calendar from destinationCalendar.externalId.

For bookings whose stored reference has no externalCalendarId (all pre-refactor bookings, and the fallback path where CalendarManager returns externalId undefined), calendar.events.update receives no calendarId, Google rejects the call, and rescheduling/edits of existing bookings fail with a Google API error where the old code resolved the calendar from destinationCalendar.externalId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null/undefined`), the `find` compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value, which will not match normal calendar IDs, yielding `undefined`. That means the update will not target the event’s destination calendar (it will either pass `undefined` or fall back elsewhere depending on code not shown in the snippet), breaking updates for events created on a non-primary calendar when the stored reference lacks `externalCalendarId`. The same flawed pattern is also introduced in `deleteEvent`’s `calendarId` computation.
